content.value: PDS Wave 19 — Arm the Crown Cleanly and Fire It: the state is finally aligned, so the honest outcome is a fired climb

Living wave Paper for wave 19 of the Personal Development Server epic (root task pds-w1-crown-proof). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md (PDS-D1..D267). This Paper is the wave's living story — Digest appends the survey digest before the verifiers fly, Decide appends the wave plan before the builders fly, Review closes it as the debrief. Fan-out workers never write this Paper; each Fable phase folds their bp-task reports in.
Status

VERIFYING. The Fable digest folded 17 survey reports; the state the wish describes is L1-confirmed and the honest outcome is a FIRED climb, not a refusal. A tight 6-assignment verify fleet is now in flight to PROVE the load-bearing claims by running (not reading) before Decide cuts the arm slice. Under the RESTORED-FABLE policy this wave's thinking phases are Fable and builders default to Fable.
The wish

THIS CYCLE: PDS WAVE 19 — ARM THE CROWN CLEANLY AND FIRE IT. Wave 18 booted the scratch target (it is STILL ALIVE) and armed a climb, but the climb failed step 0b (deploy-provenance) because the lead was merging PRs that moved guerrilla's HEAD out from under the fire worktree. The lead has now FROZEN all merges. Everything is finally aligned: scratch alive, memory window open, 0b viable. Arm a fresh detached climb and let it fire. Root task: pds-w1-crown-proof.
Where the crown stands: 9 of 12

The crown proof (pds-w1-crown-proof) carries 12 acceptance criteria. Criteria 0-5 and 7-9 are MET from earlier climbs. Unmet: 6 (content-and-presence convergence across a real reboot, with a deliberate 8-column sentinel and a guard-off control), 10 (PR merged — LEAD closes on merge, merge-gated, never stamped early per PDS-D163), and 11 (the SINGLE-RUN ATTRIBUTION FENCE — every criterion 0-10 must cite ONE IDENTICAL run_id, or the crown is explicitly REFUSED naming the rung that failed). Criterion 11 is the whole game: the currently-met criteria carry NO shared run_id, so a fresh serial climb must re-green ALL rungs 0-9 under one run_id, and the LEAD then re-stamps 0-10 to that id and seals 11 last-and-alone. A mosaic is not a crown.
The direction: ARM CLEAN, FIRE ONCE

Reuse the LIVE c7528814 scratch target — it is alive (curl http://127.0.0.1:37576/api/schemas -> 200), and, measured this turn, its schema is BYTE-IDENTICAL to guerrilla's deployed sha (ZERO migrations between the scratch's origin sha 6782db5d and guerrilla 34b9b25d; reboot.log reads 'Migrations already up'), so rung-1's COPY of guerrilla data will not fail on any CHECK/enum widening (the PDS-D32 hazard does not bite). Cut a FRESH fire worktree at the frozen origin/main HEAD (58862f62); guerrilla's deployed sha 34b9b25d is its ancestor, so rung 0b holds, and because the lead has FROZEN all merges guerrilla settles at <= that sha and stays inside the epoch. Re-read /tmp/pds-full-export/attempts (4) and set PDS_FULL_EXPORT_BUDGET = spent+2 = 6 in ONE contiguous shell at fire time (reuse is DEAD: the parked 1.4 GB bundle's served_sha 8eeaf688 is stale, so PDS-D223's provenance gate refuses it and rungs 3/4 take one FRESH full export = attempt 5 of 6). Arm scripts/pds-crown-launch.sh DETACHED with the frozen harness, floor 2200 UNSET, --prewarm-now, --max-draws 2160 --interval 10 (a 6 h window). Record run_id/run_tag/pid/transcript/budget/scratch-home in a fire RECORD, push, and END THE TURN — no polling.

THE REUSE LINCHPIN (measured this turn): cmd_arm's detached child sets BARKPARK_HOME=/tmp/pds-w14.$run_tag UNCONDITIONALLY, where run_tag = cksum(PDS_RUN_ID); it does NOT honor a pre-exported BARKPARK_HOME. So the ONLY way to point the climb at the live scratch home /tmp/pds-w14.c7528814 is to arm with the exact PDS_RUN_ID whose cksum yields c7528814. That id is RECOVERED: PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw18-crown (verified: printf pdsw18-crown | cksum -> c7528814). This is not the harness-internal transcript run_id (criterion 0 cites a timestamp id like 20260720T032558Z-28651), which is minted fresh per run — so reusing pdsw18-crown to hit the live home does NOT muddy the single-run fence; the wave-19 climb still produces a fresh attribution id.

The finished experience: a detached child outlives the turn, pre-warms the prod compile off the clock, polls up to 6 h for a MemAvailable >= 2200 MiB window, FIRES on the first high-regime draw (the window is open NOW at ~2380-2420 MiB), takes ONE fresh full export (the deployed spill engine's real peak is ~477 MiB, so 2200 is hugely conservative and prod stays healthy — empirically true from wave 16's 1.4 GB fire at 2578 MiB), and greens the whole ladder under ONE run_id. OR it stands down honestly — draws exhausted, or a FIRE-then-immediate cond_b refusal — spending zero attempts. Per PDS-D262 there are THREE honest outcomes; given the alignment, the honest EXPECTATION is a fired climb, not a refusal. The LEAD then collects (six named states, ps -p never pgrep; the PDS-D261 bundle cross-check before any stamp) and seals: re-stamp criteria 0-9 to the ONE wave-19 run_id, 10 on merge with the SHA recorded, 11 LAST and ALONE (which also disarms the cmux Stop-hook false-close).
The direction debate

RIVAL A — ARM CLEAN, FIRE ONCE (WINNER). Reuse the live scratch, cut a fresh fire tree at frozen origin/main, arm detached with the recovered run_id, return. One round-1 slice; a round-2 LEAD-only seal. ZERO new scripts.

RIVAL B — HARDEN THE LAUNCHER FIRST. Teach cmd_arm to boot and assert scratch.env at its derived home, and fix the stale-PDS_SCRATCH_TREE class, THEN fire (the backlog task pds-bl-launcher-assert-scratch-env). Durable, but PDS-D266 explicitly DEFERRED it: a launcher edit makes the fire round-2 and delays the seal, against the finish mandate and ZERO-NEW-SCRIPTS. It forecloses nothing — the class-fix is filed and lands AFTER the crown fires.

RIVAL C — DISTRUST THE REUSE; BOOT A FRESH SCRATCH AT THE FIRE TREE. Cleaner attribution and guaranteed tree/schema coherence, but it pays a boot (Postgres + prod compile, ~188 s cold) whose memory contention competes with the export, and it abandons the alignment the lead worked to establish; the memory window could slam shut during the boot. Its ONLY real advantage — schema coherence — is removed by the measurement that the scratch schema is already byte-identical to guerrilla (0 migrations in range).

WHY A WON: the state is aligned at L1 RIGHT NOW — scratch alive, schema identical to guerrilla, memory window open, 0b viable under the freeze. Every hour of hardening (B) or re-booting (C) is an hour the lead's merge-freeze holds the entire repo hostage and an hour the window can close. A fires within minutes of a high-regime draw. The finish mandate, ZERO-NEW-SCRIPTS, and the explicit 'reuse the live target' instruction all point at A.

SHARPEST ATTACK ON A, AND HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT: reuse imports guerrilla data into a scratch migrated from a STALE tree (6782db5d, behind guerrilla) whose recorded PDS_SCRATCH_TREE (in scratch.env) points at the stale w18-fire tree — so rung 0b could REPRODUCE the exact wave-18 ancestry failure (git-ancestry of a recorded tree, not a schema check), and rung 1's COPY could fail on a schema widening. ABSORBED: (1) the COPY hazard is dissolved by measurement — ZERO migrations between 6782db5d and guerrilla 34b9b25d, schemas byte-identical, reboot.log 'Migrations already up'; (2) the 0b ancestry residue is the #1 survey question — the wave must confirm which tree rung 0b compares against and, if it sources PDS_SCRATCH_TREE from scratch.env, re-point that at the fresh fire tree (58862f62) before arming — a one-line env fix, not a reboot. SECOND ATTACK: single-shot — a fresh export (attempt 5/6) that fires but reds rung 3/4 for a non-0b reason burns the attempt for another honest-partial. ABSORBED: the export is empirically prod-safe (wave 16, 1.4 GB at 2578 MiB, prod healthy, spill peak ~477 MiB); the 2200 floor + cond_b gate fires only in a high window; and STANDING LAW sorts any red as HARNESS BUG or ENGINE FAIL — filed, honest, ledger-advancing. A named refusal is a win.
The survey plan

A wide net of Sonnet surveyors, each answering one concrete question that either confirms the aligned state at L1 or arms the builder brief. The load-bearing assumptions surfaced by the stress-test are all represented. Key questions:

1. zerob-tree-source (THE CRUX) — which tree does rung 0b in pds-pull-proof.sh compare guerrilla's deployed sha against: the tree the harness RUNS from (fresh fire tree 58862f62), or PDS_SCRATCH_TREE from scratch.env (currently the stale w18-fire tree 6782db5d, which would reproduce the wave-18 0b failure)? If the latter, the fire slice re-points PDS_SCRATCH_TREE at the fresh tree before arming.

2. schema-coverage — re-read guerrilla's live deployed sha over SSH at survey time; confirm ZERO migrations / no CHECK/enum widening between the scratch's actual schema and that sha, so rung-1 COPY cannot fail on constraints.

3. reuse-handle — verify PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw18-crown derives run_tag c7528814 -> BARKPARK_HOME=/tmp/pds-w14.c7528814 = live scratch; confirm the child ignores a pre-exported BARKPARK_HOME so run_id is the ONLY reuse handle.

4. scratch-liveness-and-cleanliness — re-confirm curl 37576 == 200; is the scratch DB clean (did wave-18's climb stop at 0b before rung-1's pull, leaving no half-imported data), or does it carry residue the ladder must reset?

5. arm-interface — the exact arm invocation: flags, env to UNSET (PDS_LAUNCH_HARNESS, PDS_AMMO_FILE, PDS_FULL_EXPORT_MIN_MEM_MB, PDS_LAUNCH_MEM_FLOOR_MIB), env to SET (PDS_CONTROL_PG=postgres; PDS_LAUNCH_HARNESS -> the fresh worktree's pds-pull-proof.sh), how fire_detached computes budget=spent+2, and how child.sh line 7 must equal the fire tree's harness (PDS-D259).
6. frozen-harness-blob — confirm scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh blob at origin/main (e219e97c) IS the known-frozen blob wave 15/16/18 climbed; git-log the blob for any drift.
7. budget-attempts — confirm attempts reads 4, the parked bundle's served_sha is stale (8eeaf688) so PDS-D223 refuses it -> fresh export; budget spent+2=6; gate (c) spent<budget holds.

8. stack-guard-and-locks — confirm no live climber (wave-18 child pid 83700 dead, STATE_DIR/last=c7528814); will re-arming at run_tag c7528814 need --force, or does cmd_arm's guard proceed on the dead pid? Check the stranded mkdir export lock /tmp/pds-full-export/lock.
9. memory-window — sample MemAvailable over a few minutes over SSH; is the >=2200 window open now; how cond_b (b) samples; 2160 draws x 10 s = 6 h; the three honest outcomes.
10. criterion-11-runid — what exact string is the transcript 'run_id' the criteria cite (harness-internal timestamp vs PDS_RUN_ID)? Confirms reusing pdsw18-crown does not muddy the single-run fence.

11. stamp-recipe — read scripts/pds-crown-stamp.sh: fetch-to-file, pass criterion text by "$(cat f)" (6 has literal backticks, 5/6/11 have single quotes), re-stamp ALL 0-9 to one run_id, 10 on merge, 11 last-and-alone; PDS-D163 no-early-stamp; cmux Stop-hook false-close disarm.

12. rungs-3-4-full-export — map rungs 3 and 4 (the only full-bundle consumers): acquire_full_bundle, the D223 provenance gate, gates (a)-(e), the 1 Hz ps RSS sampler, and how a red there sorts HARNESS-BUG vs ENGINE-FAIL.

13. wave-18-debrief — read paper pds-wave-18-2026-07-21 + task pds-w18-crown-fire: how far did wave-18's climb get, did it burn attempt 3->4, what exactly failed, and is anything else stranded (worktrees, locks).

14. severability-D71 — confirm the ladder is severable (dev rungs run regardless of the full-export gate) so a headroom ABORT costs two rungs, not the crown core; which rungs need only the cheap dev export.

15. detach-form — confirm the python3 fork+setsid+execvp detach form works on this host (no setsid/nohup), the child survives turn-end, closerange keeps arm non-hanging, and collect reads the six states via ps -p.

16. concurrent-contention — are any OTHER PDS climbs, foreign worktrees, or session agents (spill-*, pt-*, janitor-fix, icon-fix) touching the scratch target, the attempts file, the export lock, or guerrilla right now? Scan open PRs + worktrees + processes to avoid a collision.

17. lead-collect-brief — precisely what criteria 10 and 11 need so the LEAD collects and seals in ONE step: the six collect states, the D261 bundle cross-check (file / tar -tf / manifest profile==full) before any stamp, the exact re-stamp set (ALL 0-9), 10-on-merge-with-SHA, 11-last-and-alone.
Standing law for this wave

ZERO NEW SCRIPTS — every instrument is merged (pds-crown-launch.sh, pds-pull-proof.sh FROZEN at e219e97c, pds-export-peak-measure.sh, pds-idle-sampler.sh, pds-crown-stamp.sh). Permitted new artifacts: the fire RECORD, TRANSCRIPT, DERIVATION, and this Paper/charter text. FENCE: scripts/pds-* ONLY — do NOT touch tooling/grip/, cloud/, or api/** (FROZEN for the crown). Never lower the frozen 2200 floor; report ATTEMPTS not successes; MiB = kB/1024; indices zero-based; every red sorts HARNESS-BUG or ENGINE-FAIL, both filed, neither fixed mid-proof; never manufacture a restart or request a deploy. The reviewer pushes the fire record + Paper (pushed=true), but the LEAD will not merge until the crown fires — the CLIMB is what matters.
Survey digest — what 17 reports established

The wish's premise holds and is corroborated at L1 by multiple independent surveyors: the scratch target c7528814 is ALIVE (curl 127.0.0.1:37576 -> 200; PG on 42428, beam alive); reuse handle PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw18-crown -> cksum -> run_tag c7528814 -> BARKPARK_HOME=/tmp/pds-w14.c7528814 (the launcher exports this UNCONDITIONALLY, the ONLY handle onto the live home — fire_detached at pds-crown-launch.sh:197); the frozen harness blob is e219e97ccf7f33797c86a2b84d998d599b6bda31, unchanged since wave 8 (git rev-parse origin/main:scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh, PDS-D146); attempts reads 4 so PDS_FULL_EXPORT_BUDGET must be exported = spent+2 = 6 in the SAME shell; the parked bundle served_sha 8eeaf688 is stale vs guerrilla 34b9b25d so PDS-D223 refuses reuse and a fresh export = attempt 5/6; the ladder is severable (PDS-D71): 9 rungs run on the cheap dev export, only rungs 3 and 4 consume the one full bundle; the python3 fork+setsid+execvp detach form (closerange 3-64, ANSI-C quoting) is shipped and self-tested.

THREE CORRECTIONS to the strategic direction, each landing on the winner's attack lines. (1) Rung 0b does NOT read PDS_SCRATCH_TREE. worktree_sha comes from REPO_ROOT, derived purely from $0 (the harness's own invocation path) at pds-pull-proof.sh:88-89, then rev-parse HEAD at :642; DEPLOYED_SHA is a live SSH to guerrilla /opt/barkpark at :562. The direction's 'absorb 0b by re-pointing PDS_SCRATCH_TREE' step is moot — the ONLY lever is invoking pds-crown-launch.sh BY PATH FROM the fresh worktree so $0 resolves REPO_ROOT to it. No env fix. (2) 'guerrilla 34b9b25d is an ancestor of the scratch origin sha 6782db5d' is FALSE — they are unmerged siblings, neither is an ancestor of the other (6782db5d lives only on origin/pds/w18-fire). The rung-1 COPY hazard is dissolved anyway, but by a DIFFERENT mechanism: the api/priv/repo/migrations subtree is BYTE-IDENTICAL between the two shas (git diff --stat empty, 182 files identical). The Paper must cite migrations-subtree-identity, not ancestry. The separate 0b claim (guerrilla 34b9b25d IS an ancestor of fire-worktree HEAD 58862f62) DOES hold. (3) PDS_LAUNCH_HARNESS must be UNSET, never exported (PDS-D259: 'setting it IS the failure mode'); invoked by-path from the fresh worktree the default resolves correctly (child.sh line 7 == the fresh worktree's pds-pull-proof.sh).

THE ONE UNADDRESSED HAZARD — the transcript / STATE-DIR append collision. Reusing run_tag c7528814 reuses it for the launcher's OWN state dir /tmp/pds-crown-launch/c7528814/ too, not just BARKPARK_HOME. That dir ALREADY holds a COMPLETE FAILED wave-18 transcript (RESULT: FAIL / EXIT: 1, 70 draws; full ladder ran: 0a PASS, 0b FAIL, 0c PASS, 1 PASS, 2 PASS, 3/4 ABORT, 5/6/7 PASS, 8 FAIL on the deploy storm f34052df->34b9b25d). fire_detached opens transcript.log with O_APPEND and never truncates; classify()/collect() grep the WHOLE file for ^EXIT:/^RESULT:, so from the moment a re-arm exists collect reads FINISHED off the STALE wave-18 lines while wave-19 is still climbing, and any top-down scrape of 'PASS 0a'/'SUMMARY — run c7528814' grabs wave-18's FAIL. This is exactly the mosaic criterion 11 (the single-run attribution fence) exists to forbid, and NO PDS-D covers it. Decide MUST rule one of: (a) archive/move-aside /tmp/pds-crown-launch/c7528814/{transcript.log,child.pid,meta} before arming, or (b) export a fresh PDS_LAUNCH_STATE_DIR while keeping PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw18-crown for BARKPARK_HOME reuse (STATE_DIR's root is independently overridable). Meta/child.pid/child.sh truncate cleanly on re-arm; only transcript.log appends. Wave 18's child pid 83700 is DEAD, so re-arm needs no --force.

THE DIRTY SCRATCH DB. The scratch is NOT virgin: it carries wave-18's dev-profile merge-pull of guerrilla content (3572 documents, 15,859 rows across 13 tables) PLUS 34 config rows whose guarded columns were deliberately clobbered to Bootstrap defaults by rung-6's guard-off control, PLUS workspaces.settings->pull_provenance[production] currently reads {} (empty) despite that real pull. A wave-19 fresh full-profile --merge pull SHOULD overwrite the residue and re-stamp provenance (PDS-D14 idempotent-refresh), but rung-2 (count-diff) and rung-6 (convergence) must be measured against wave-19's OWN fresh pull, never this residue. Open: does pds-scratch-target.sh 'up --verify' reset pgdata or reuse it — determines whether an explicit reset is needed.

MEMORY WINDOW — thinner than the headline. The direction/lead cite ~2378-2420 MiB; two independent survey samplings measured 2200-2270 (one sample only 0.36 MiB over the 2200 floor) and 2250-2258. The window is OPEN but thin, so outcome C (launcher draw gate clears, then the harness's own cond_b re-samples seconds later and refuses) is a real possibility. It does NOT block arming — the detached child polls up to 6h (2160 draws x 10s) and a closed gate costs ZERO export attempts. Floor stays 2200, no asterisk (fresh export real RAM peak ~477 MiB; wave-16 fired 1.4 GB at 2578 MiB and prod stayed healthy).

FREEZE IS A CONVENTION, NOT A GATE. origin/main sat stationary at 58862f62 across repeated fetches and guerrilla stayed at 34b9b25d, consistent with the lead's merge freeze holding. But no branch-protection/CI gate enforces it, and 4 open+mergeable non-PDS PRs touch the auto-deploy trigger set (api/** #5482, cloud/priv/static/** #5478-5480) — any one merging mid-climb reproduces the wave-18 deploy-storm failure at 0b/8. Operator discipline; the only in-flight guard is rung 0a/8's live sha re-pin AFTER the fact.

Decide — Verification Results (the deep round)

PROVEN. (1) The one unaddressed hazard is REAL on disk: /tmp/pds-crown-launch/c7528814/transcript.log carries wave-18's COMPLETE FAILED run (554 lines, terminal 'RESULT: FAIL' / 'EXIT: 1'), and `collect c7528814` reads STATE: FINISHED off it RIGHT NOW; fire_detached opens the log O_APPEND (line 200) and classify greps the whole file — a re-arm would scrape the stale FAIL. A tight 6-assignment verify fleet is now in flight to PROVE the load-bearing claims by running (not reading) before Decide cuts the arm slice. Under the RESTORED-FABLE policy this wave's thinking phases are Fable and builders default to Fable.

The wish

THIS CYCLE: PDS WAVE 19 — ARM THE CROWN CLEANLY AND FIRE IT. Wave 18 booted the scratch target (it is STILL ALIVE) and armed a climb, but the climb failed step 0b (deploy-provenance) because the lead was merging PRs that moved guerrilla's HEAD out from under the fire worktree. The lead has now FROZEN all merges. Everything is finally aligned: scratch alive, memory window open, 0b viable. Arm a fresh detached climb and let it fire. Root task: pds-w1-crown-proof.

Where the crown stands: 9 of 12

The crown proof (pds-w1-crown-proof) carries 12 acceptance criteria. Criteria 0-5 and 7-9 are MET from earlier climbs. Unmet: 6 (content-and-presence convergence across a real reboot, with a deliberate 8-column sentinel and a guard-off control), 10 (PR merged — LEAD closes on merge, merge-gated, never stamped early per PDS-D163), and 11 (the SINGLE-RUN ATTRIBUTION FENCE — every criterion 0-10 must cite ONE IDENTICAL run_id, or the crown is explicitly REFUSED naming the rung that failed). Criterion 11 is the whole game: the currently-met criteria carry NO shared run_id, so a fresh serial climb must re-green ALL rungs 0-9 under one run_id, and the LEAD then re-stamps 0-10 to that id and seals 11 last-and-alone. A mosaic is not a crown.

The direction: ARM CLEAN, FIRE ONCE

Reuse the LIVE c7528814 scratch target — it is alive (curl http://127.0.0.1:37576/api/schemas -> 200), and, measured this turn, its schema is BYTE-IDENTICAL to guerrilla's deployed sha (ZERO migrations between the scratch's origin sha 6782db5d and guerrilla 34b9b25d; reboot.log reads 'Migrations already up'), so rung-1's COPY of guerrilla data will not fail on any CHECK/enum widening (the PDS-D32 hazard does not bite). Cut a FRESH fire worktree at the frozen origin/main HEAD (58862f62); guerrilla's deployed sha 34b9b25d is its ancestor, so rung 0b holds, and because the lead has FROZEN all merges guerrilla settles at <= that sha and stays inside the epoch. Re-read /tmp/pds-full-export/attempts (4) and set PDS_FULL_EXPORT_BUDGET = spent+2 = 6 in ONE contiguous shell at fire time (reuse is DEAD: the parked 1.4 GB bundle's served_sha 8eeaf688 is stale, so PDS-D223's provenance gate refuses it and rungs 3/4 take one FRESH full export = attempt 5 of 6). Arm scripts/pds-crown-launch.sh DETACHED with the frozen harness, floor 2200 UNSET, --prewarm-now, --max-draws 2160 --interval 10 (a 6 h window). Record run_id/run_tag/pid/transcript/budget/scratch-home in a fire RECORD, push, and END THE TURN — no polling.

THE REUSE LINCHPIN (measured this turn): cmd_arm's detached child sets BARKPARK_HOME=/tmp/pds-w14.$run_tag UNCONDITIONALLY, where run_tag = cksum(PDS_RUN_ID); it does NOT honor a pre-exported BARKPARK_HOME. So the ONLY way to point the climb at the live scratch home /tmp/pds-w14.c7528814 is to arm with the exact PDS_RUN_ID whose cksum yields c7528814. That id is RECOVERED: PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw18-crown (verified: printf pdsw18-crown | cksum -> c7528814). This is not the harness-internal transcript run_id (criterion 0 cites a timestamp id like 20260720T032558Z-28651), which is minted fresh per run — so reusing pdsw18-crown to hit the live home does NOT muddy the single-run fence; the wave-19 climb still produces a fresh attribution id.

The finished experience: a detached child outlives the turn, pre-warms the prod compile off the clock, polls up to 6 h for a MemAvailable >= 2200 MiB window, FIRES on the first high-regime draw (the window is open NOW at ~2380-2420 MiB), takes ONE fresh full export (the deployed spill engine's real peak is ~477 MiB, so 2200 is hugely conservative and prod stays healthy — empirically true from wave 16's 1.4 GB fire at 2578 MiB), and greens the whole ladder under ONE run_id. OR it stands down honestly — draws exhausted, or a FIRE-then-immediate cond_b refusal — spending zero attempts. Per PDS-D262 there are THREE honest outcomes; given the alignment, the honest EXPECTATION is a fired climb, not a refusal. The LEAD then collects (six named states, ps -p never pgrep; the PDS-D261 bundle cross-check before any stamp) and seals: re-stamp criteria 0-9 to the ONE wave-19 run_id, 10 on merge with the SHA recorded, 11 LAST and ALONE (which also disarms the cmux Stop-hook false-close).

WHY A WON: the state is aligned at L1 RIGHT NOW — scratch alive, schema identical to guerrilla, memory window open, 0b viable under the freeze. Every hour of hardening (B) or re-booting (C) is an hour the lead's merge-freeze holds the entire repo hostage and an hour the window can close. A fires within minutes of a high-regime draw. ABSORBED: the export is empirically prod-safe (wave 16, 1.4 GB at 2578 MiB, prod healthy, spill peak ~477 MiB); the 2200 floor + cond_b gate fires only in a high window; and STANDING LAW sorts any red as HARNESS BUG or ENGINE FAIL — filed, honest, ledger-advancing.
